text:
Maya Chen: quick sync — we're picking a global default for token fallback/waterfall when multiple creds are present. current implicit behavior is org_key -> project_key -> service_account. that ordering is causing surprising quota attribution and SLA oddities for burrito customers.
Samir Patel: surprised — I thought we were doing project_key first (to respect project-level quotas). where is org_key winning?
Maya Chen: it happens when requests come from our internal proxy that attaches an org-level credential earlier in the call chain. service teams see org quota consumed even though they intended project scoped.
Alex Gomez: that explains the telemetry spikes in /dash/team-quotas yesterday. we saw high token counts attributed to org:acme even when project:acme-web should've taken it.
Jordan Lee: can we change to project -> sa -> org? that feels logical: prefer narrower scope first.
Priya Rao: UX/console question: if we change ordering, how do we show which cred actually fulfilled the request? customers are going to ask why their org quota stopped.
Samir Patel: add an auth_source tag on every request metric: auth_source=project|service_account|org. dashboard filter. minimal perf cost.
Maya Chen: agreed. also need audits/logs: auth_path list so ops can replay decision. e.g., auth_path=[header_project_key, cookie_sa, header_org_key].
Alex Gomez: implementable. small concern: changing fallback order affects SLA/backward compatibility. some teams rely on org-level rate limits being enforced before project limits.
Jordan Lee: which SLA? our Hosted API SLO is per-customer latency/availability. quota enforcement order shouldn't change latency but may change throttling behavior.
Samir Patel: it's a behavioral change — customers using org key for cross-project burst protection will suddenly bypass org throttles if project key present. could lead to overruns.
Priya Rao: rollouts UX: we should ship as feature-flagged canary with visible telemetry. propose header: `X-Auth-Fallback-Canary: true` and a console toggle per org for the new fallback.
Maya Chen: outline plan: 1) implement telemetry tag + auth_path logs 2) default fallback -> project,sa,org behind canary 3) run canary on internal orgs + selected customers 4) observe quota attribution for 7 days 5) opt-in console toggle then full rollout.
Alex Gomez: +1. Dev note: minimal config snippet I sketched:
```
auth:
  fallback_order: ["project", "service_account", "org"]
  emit_auth_source_metric: true
```
Samir Patel: also add a safety net: when project quota would exceed threshold, fallback to org to prevent 429 storms. basically a conditional waterfall with threshold checks.
Jordan Lee: hmm conditional logic adds complexity. But we can do a simple rule: if project_quota_remaining < X tokens, check org quota instead. what X? maybe 5% of project burst capacity.
Priya Rao: console needs to expose both the effective key and the evaluated ruleset that triggered fallback. small UX: show `effective_key` and `evaluated_rules` on request inspector.
Maya Chen: operational telemetry: add two new dashboards: "Quota Attribution by Auth Source" and "Fallback Hits (project->org)". set alerts if fallback from project->org exceeds 5% of traffic during canary.
infra-bot: deploy-job #auth-fallback-canary started by maya.eta — logs: https://ci/reports/2147859123
Alex Gomez: can we inject a canary header so we don't need console toggles for initial testing? like `x-auth-fallback=canary` that triggers new codepath.
Samir Patel: yep that's the plan. then we flip a feature flag server-side for orgs that opt into canary.
Jordan Lee: timeline? I'd like a 2-week canary + 1 week observation before broad opt-in.
Maya Chen: timeline sounds good. action items: Samir -> implement metrics + threshold rule prototype. Alex -> dashboard + alert queries. Priya -> console inspector mock. Jordan -> update canary runbook. I'll own rollout comms.
Samir Patel: on it. I'll PR with metric names: `auth_source`, `auth_path`, `fallback_reason`.
Priya Rao: will mock inspector today, sample UI text ready by EOD.
Maya Chen: thanks everyone. :thumbsup: we'll reconvene after initial telemetry baseline (48h).
